item.title: A Weekend For Proof
item.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. That development changes the context of the coming days. Electoral preparation now requires visible progress on protection, accountability and public confidence alongside equipment and political agreements. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? How long did uploads take? How were exceptions resolved? A rehearsal can reveal problems that announcements cannot. Finding a fault early allows INEC to correct it. Explaining that correction gives citizens a reason to have greater confidence. The exercise also has practical support from state governments. Lagos has cancelled Saturday’s sanitation exercise, while Anambra has postponed its own, to avoid obstructing participation. Those decisions remove an immediate obstacle. The remaining test concerns delivery at the selected polling units. Monday: What Will Opposition Unity Require? Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Seyi Makinde and other opposition leaders are expected at the November 30 summit. Their attendance and any signed commitments remain forthcoming. The APC says it is untroubled by the proposed gathering. The parties’ task is to define cooperation precisely. Joint election monitoring could be valuable. So could common procedures for documenting intimidation, sharing verified information and coordinating legal responses. Presidential cooperation presents more difficult choices. Supporters need to know whether their parties intend to campaign separately, endorse an existing candidate or pursue another lawful arrangement. A declaration of unity leaves those questions open unless it specifies obligations.

item.title: Ogun 2027: Court dismisses Hunye’s suits against Adeola’s APC candidacy
item.description: …Adeola hails judgment …as Hunye heads to Court of Appeal By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Federal High Court sitting in Abeokuta, Ogun State, on Friday dismissed two suits filed by Hon. Abayomi Semako Hunye challenging the emergence of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, as the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 election. Delivering judgment in the two consolidated suits, Justice Okeke held that the cases lacked merit and consequently dismissed them. The suits, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1127/2026 and FHC/AB/126/2026, were instituted by Hunye against the APC, Senator Adeola and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), challenging the process through which Adeola emerged as the party’s governorship candidate. Reacting to the judgment, Adeola commended the judiciary, describing the decision as a vindication of the rule of law and the judicial process. In a statement issued by his media adviser, Chief Kayode Odunaro, the senator expressed satisfaction with the outcome while appreciating his legal team for what he described as their painstaking efforts in defending the suits. Adeola said, “I want to commend the Honourable Justice for his erudite judgment in these cases challenging my overwhelming and widely accepted victory in our party primary. I also commend my legal team for the painstaking defense put up during the process. “This victory is yet another milestone in our quest for equity and justice in the Ogun State 2027 election. To God be the glory once again.” The senator said that despite the legal challenges, he had remained focused on consolidating support for his candidacy across the state through engagements with political stakeholders and other interest groups. He added that his engagements had also included the presentation of his nine-pillar ITESIWAJU Agenda, which he described as his development blueprint for Ogun State. According to him, the court’s decision would allow him to concentrate more fully on preparations for the 2027 governorship election and take his campaign message to voters across the state. Adeola also urged APC members and his supporters, irrespective of their political affiliations, to remain united and focused, stressing that his ambition was driven by a desire to serve the people and contribute to the development of Ogun State. However, Hunye has rejected the outcome of the proceedings and indicated his intention to appeal the judgment. In a statement titled, “Our Legal Journey Continues to the Court of Appeal,” Hunye described the Federal High Court as the first stage of the judicial process, insisting that the appellate court would provide another opportunity for his legal team to pursue the issues raised in the suits. He reaffirmed his commitment to constitutional due process, internal party democracy, and the rule of law, saying his decision to continue with the litigation was informed by the need to ensure fairness and strict compliance with establi

item.title: Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand
item.description: Two Nigerian men have been arrested in Thailand over their alleged links to an international romance scam network targeting victims across Southeast Asia. The suspects, aged 41 and 30, were arrested on November 18 at a condominium in Ban Mai, Pak Kret district, Nonthaburi, following an investigation by Thailand’s Immigration Division 3 and Provincial Police Region 1. According to local media outlet, The Thaiger, undercover police officers disguised themselves as food delivery workers to gain access to the suspects’ apartment. With the help of security guards, the officers approached the condominium and pretended to have a parcel for delivery. When one of the men opened the door, they identified themselves as police officers and moved in to arrest both suspects. A search of the apartment reportedly led to the recovery of laptops and mobile phones containing messages linked to fake online identities posing as US military personnel. Investigators suspect the identities were used to establish romantic relationships with potential victims as part of an international scam operation. Police also reportedly found social media accounts allegedly created to deceive Thai residents. The arrests followed an earlier investigation on November 12, when police detained another Nigerian man, aged 37, at Owl Market in Nonthaburi over suspected links to the same network. Investigators later searched a condominium in Bang Kraso, Mueang Nonthaburi, where suspected members of the group had reportedly stayed. However, the men had left before the search. Police subsequently traced the two suspects to another condominium in the Muang Thong Thani area, where they were believed to have stayed for two to three days before their arrest. The Thaiger reported that both men confessed during questioning. However, the charges publicly reported against them are immigration-related offences, including illegal entry and unauthorised residence. One of the suspects, aged 41, had reportedly overstayed his permitted stay in Thailand by 411 days. Authorities revoked their permission to remain in the country and transferred them to Pak Kret Police Station for further legal proceedings ahead of deportation. The investigation into the suspected romance scam network is ongoing. Thai police have not disclosed the identities of the alleged victims, the amount of money involved or the specific roles the two men allegedly played in the operation. The reported immigration charges do not amount to convictions for romance fraud. The post Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Adesua Etomi celebrates negative cancer test
item.description: Nollywood actress Adesua Etomi-Wellington has celebrated testing negative for cancer after months of medical procedures, hospital visits and uncertainty over her health. The actress announced the development on Friday in an Instagram video, expressing gratitude to God following the latest result from her medical tests. “The doctor just called me back with the result from the lab, no cancer… God is good,” she said. The video showed some of the medical procedures she underwent, while other pictures revealed bruises on her body and redness beneath one of her eyes. Etomi-Wellington also shared a video of friends and well-wishers celebrating the result with her. Reflecting on her experience, the actress described 2026 as one of the most difficult periods of her life, explaining that her reduced public appearances were linked to her health struggles. “2026 really tried it. I know I’ve been quieter than usual this year (and that’s saying something), but behind the silence were some of the most difficult months of my life,” she wrote. She disclosed that the ordeal involved several medical procedures, scans, injections and hospital visits, adding that she received treatment from medical teams in Nigeria and the United States. “This year threw everything at me, but by the grace of God, I am NOT EASILY BROKEN,” she added. The actress also expressed appreciation to her husband, singer and politician Bankole Wellington, popularly known as Banky W, their children, friends and family members for supporting her throughout the difficult period. “To my friends and family who prayed for me, stood in the gap and held me through some of my darkest days, I will never take your love for granted,” she wrote. The health update comes two days after the couple released a gospel song, On My Way , on November 25 to celebrate their ninth wedding anniversary. The track, credited to Etomi-Wellington, who performs under the musical name Susu, and Banky W, is the lead single from their forthcoming joint album, Not Easily Broken , expected in 2027. The actress described the song as “the soundtrack to our testimony and thanksgiving”, linking its message to their personal experiences. The couple have previously spoken about their health challenges. In May 2024, Banky W disclosed that he had undergone his fourth surgery for cancer after earlier procedures to remove cancerous tumours. Etomi-Wellington also revealed in March 2025 that she battled hyperemesis gravidarum, a severe form of pregnancy sickness, during her second pregnancy. The condition left her ill for months and required hospitalisation before she underwent an emergency Caesarean section. The post Adesua Etomi celebrates negative cancer test appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UK lists two conditions for bringing goods into country without paying tax
item.description: The United Kingdom government has outlined two conditions under which travellers can bring goods into the country without paying customs duty or tax, warning that items outside the permitted categories or allowance limits could attract charges. According to the UK government’s customs guidelines, travellers can bring goods into the country tax-free under two conditions. First condition is personal use. Goods must be intended for the traveller’s own use rather than for commercial purposes or resale. Second condition is gifts. Travellers can also bring goods intended as presents for other people without paying customs duty, provided they remain within the applicable personal allowance. The rules apply to foreign visitors and British residents returning from overseas, regardless of whether the items were purchased from regular shops or duty-free outlets at airports. However, the exemptions are subject to personal allowance limits, which determine the quantity and value of goods travellers can bring into the country without incurring additional charges. The applicable allowance depends on where a traveller is arriving from and whether the destination is Great Britain, comprising England, Scotland and Wales, or Northern Ireland. The government also warned that goods intended for business or resale do not qualify for personal allowances. Such items must be declared to customs regardless of their value or quantity. Travellers are also required to declare goods that exceed their personal allowances or fall under banned and restricted categories before crossing the border. Declarations can be made online up to five days, or 120 hours, before arrival in the UK. The authorities warned that failure to comply with customs regulations could result in the seizure of goods and, in some cases, the vehicle used to transport them. Offenders may also face financial penalties or prosecution. The post UK lists two conditions for bringing goods into country without paying tax appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda
item.description: Trials of an experimental Ebola vaccine launched in Uganda on Friday, while a global NGO said it had bought 1.5 million doses of another candidate, as the race heats up to contain the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo strain of Ebola behind the outbreak in DRC, which has caused more than 5,700 confirmed deaths out of more than 11,000 cases since being declared in May, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Two experimental vaccines are due to start testing on Monday in the outbreak’s epicentre in eastern DRC, the WHO said, focusing on contacts of cases and people deemed at high risk of infection. But neighbouring Uganda announced it had also launched a trial of one of the vaccines, developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid pandemic. The Uganda Virus Research Institute described it as “Africa’s first mRNA Phase I clinical trial”, conducted in collaboration with Moderna. It will test 224 healthy volunteers aged between one and 65 to measure its safety and immunity potential. The other potential vaccine is the ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector vaccine developed by India’s Serum Institute and the University of Oxford — which will also begin testing in DRC on Monday. But Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, which brings together government and private donors to help developing countries acquire jabs at affordable prices, is not waiting around. After the Covid-19 pandemic, the alliance set up a new $50 million First Response Fund — under a so-called “No Regrets” approach — to allow it to buy up doses in advance even before they have been fully tested. – Deployment – Gavi signed a purchase commitment this week with the Serum Institute for 1.5 million doses of the ChAdOx1, and plans to have “hundreds of thousands” ready to deploy should the trials prove successful and they are approved by the WHO and DRC government. “We’re investing in it, hoping that the signals will be positive, and if that is the case, we’ll have gained months and months on the deployment,” Emanuele Capobianco, Gavi’s director of global health security, told AFP. He said he hoped for trials to conclude “within the first half of 2027” and even “within the first quarter” in a more optimistic scenario. Gavi also has a stockpile of 500,000 doses of an existing vaccine, Ervebo, used against the Zaire strain of Ebola, which began testing last month to see if it is also effective against Bundibugyo. Despite a long and porous border with eastern DRC, Uganda has successfully contained the virus after receiving some imported cases earlier this year. It was declared Ebola-free in August after registering 20 cases, including two deaths. The post mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria set to bid to host maiden U-17 WAFCON
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigeria is preparing to bid to host the maiden edition of the Under-17 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), as the country seeks to attract more international sporting competitions and strengthen its sports economy. The Director-General of the National Sports Commission (NSC), Bukola Olopade, disclosed this in a video shared on his X handle on Friday, saying Nigeria had already communicated its interest to the Confederation of African Football (CAF). According to Olopade, the country expressed its desire to host the competition during CAF’s General Assembly held in Abuja last weekend. “We have said to CAF that we are desirous of hosting the first Under-17 women’s championship,” he said. He explained that the move forms part of Nigeria’s ambition to move away from what he described as a consuming sports economy towards a productive one, where hosting international events would generate economic benefits for the country. “We don’t want to be a consuming sports economy; rather, we want to be a productive sports economy. We want to attract more international events where the economic impacts will be felt by the people,” Olopade added. CAF’s Executive Committee approved the introduction of the U-17 WAFCON on November 21, with the inaugural tournament scheduled to take place between March and April 2028. Qualifying matches are expected to begin in April 2027. Nigeria’s interest in hosting the competition comes amid discussions about the country’s readiness to stage major international football events. Earlier this week, FIFA President Gianni Infantino said Nigeria was not yet ready to host the men’s FIFA World Cup, although he acknowledged the country’s resources, passion and willingness to stage the competition. Infantino, however, suggested that Nigeria could demonstrate its organisational capacity by hosting smaller international football tournaments before taking on events of greater magnitude. The proposed U-17 WAFCON could therefore provide Nigeria with an opportunity to showcase its capacity to organise a continental football competition. item.title: Hackers breach US Air Force Cloud computing platform
item.description: Hackers have breached Cloud One, the United States Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, potentially exposing sensitive military, personnel and logistics data. Three people familiar with the matter told Reuters that the intrusion was discovered within the past month during efforts to upgrade the system, triggering disruptions across the platform. However, the identity of the hackers, the full extent of the breach and whether any data was stolen remain unknown. In a statement to Reuters, the US Air Force declined to discuss the security status of specific networks and systems. It said: “We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities.” A major military computing platform Launched in 2017, Cloud One was designed as a centralised platform for the Air Force’s information technology needs, bringing together services provided by four major technology companies: Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet. The platform supports dozens of applications, including systems managing personnel records, salaries, logistics and military equipment maintenance. Among the applications hosted on Cloud One are the Air Force’s Cloud-Based Command and Control system, which consolidates air defence radar and other data feeds across North America, and the Theatre Integrated Combat Munitions System, which tracks bombs and missiles at more than 200 US Air Force locations worldwide. Cloud One is regarded as one of the US military’s largest cloud computing platforms, according to two sources familiar with the matter. “A breach here is a big deal,” one of the sources told Reuters. Investigators have reportedly involved US Cyber Command, the military’s cyber warfare arm, to assess the damage. Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC) served as the platform’s prime contractor until 2025, when Leidos took over the contract. SAIC did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment, while Leidos referred questions to the Air Force. Breach disrupts military operations The intrusion has reportedly triggered several disruptions across the platform. Two sources and another person familiar with the matter said plans to migrate additional back-office applications to Cloud One, a longstanding military priority, had been suspended. Updates to applications already running on the platform were also blocked, preventing Air Force personnel from installing fixes, even as new software vulnerabilities were being disclosed across the technology industry. Another source said some users had their administrator privileges revoked. One of the sources said the hackers exploited a software vulnerability to gain access to the platform’s control plane, which manages and oversees the underlying cloud infrastructure. item.title: France slips into ‘technical recession’ after GDP revision
item.description: France’s economy has slipped into a technical recession after revised official figures showed that gross domestic product (GDP) contracted in the third quarter, extending the country’s economic decline. The National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE) said on Friday that the eurozone’s second-largest economy shrank by 0.2 per cent in the third quarter, revising its initial estimate of a 0.1 per cent contraction. The agency also revised second-quarter growth downwards to 0.02 per cent from zero per cent previously, although the figure was rounded to zero in the headline data. The revisions mean France’s economy has recorded consecutive quarterly contractions since the end of last year, meeting the conventional definition of a technical recession, which is two successive quarters of negative economic growth. The latest figures pose additional challenges for the government as it struggles to rein in the country’s budget deficit, with its target of 0.5 per cent economic growth this year now appearing increasingly difficult to achieve. The minority government is also facing difficulties securing parliamentary approval for its 2027 budget, which seeks to reduce the fiscal deficit from 5.4 per cent of GDP this year to five per cent next year. The budget debate comes five months before France’s presidential election, amid deep divisions in parliament. Reacting to the figures, Finance Minister Roland Lescure called for the speedy adoption of the budget, insisting that the five per cent deficit target was non-negotiable. “We must adopt a budget as soon as possible with a non-negotiable deficit target of 5%. It is imperative that we restore visibility for economic stakeholders,” he said. A breakdown of the third-quarter GDP figures by INSEE showed that weak domestic demand contributed to the contraction. Consumer spending rose by 0.3 per cent, but this was offset by a 0.8 per cent decline in business investment. The rebuilding of business inventories contributed 0.3 percentage points to GDP growth, following a 0.7 percentage-point reduction in the previous quarter. Foreign trade also weighed heavily on economic performance, subtracting 0.6 percentage points from output as exports fell by 1.6 per cent while imports increased by 0.1 per cent. Despite the contraction, the Bank of France said earlier in November that the economy was expected to record moderate growth in the fourth quarter. item.title: Kebbi Police probe alleged importation of political thugs
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has launched an investigation into a viral video showing suspected political thugs brandishing dangerous weapons and issuing threats capable of undermining public peace and security in the state. The command also said it had invited three persons mentioned in the video for questioning over the circumstances surrounding the presence of the suspected thugs in Kebbi State. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a statement on Friday, saying intelligence reports and preliminary scrutiny of the video identified one “Mai Barewa”, described as a notorious thug from Sokoto State, alongside other individuals wielding dangerous weapons and making threatening statements. According to Usman, the individuals were heard in the video claiming to have responded to an invitation and mentioning three persons identified as Manu Gwanna, Bashar S. A. and Khairullah Jega in connection with their presence in the state. He described the threats, particularly those directed at individuals perceived not to support the ruling party, as a potential recipe for political violence. The police spokesman said the persons mentioned and identified in the video had been invited to assist the ongoing investigation, while the command was taking steps to identify, apprehend and prosecute Mai Barewa and his accomplices. He said the police would ensure that anyone found culpable was dealt with in accordance with the law. The command reiterated its commitment to political neutrality, impartial law enforcement and the protection of all citizens, irrespective of their political affiliations. It warned that no political party, individual or group would be allowed to undermine peaceful electioneering, intimidate citizens or engage in violence under the guise of political activities. The statement noted that Kebbi had long enjoyed a peaceful political climate, which must be preserved ahead of the 2027 general elections. Consequently, the police warned political parties, their leaders, supporters and associates against recruiting, harbouring, mobilising or sponsoring suspected imported thugs, or engaging in any conduct capable of inciting violence and disrupting political stability. The command further warned that it would not allow political violence, intimidation and lawlessness to take root in the state or set a dangerous precedent ahead of the 2027 elections. It urged residents to remain calm, refrain from taking the law into their own hands and promptly report suspicious activities to the nearest police station or through the command’s designated communication channels. The police assured residents of its commitment to maintaining peace, protecting lives and property, and ensuring that all political activities in the state are conducted within the ambit of the law. item.title: 2027: Nasarawa translates INEC messages into local languages
item.description: Government targets rural communities ahead of Saturday’s mock exercise By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has commenced the translation and dissemination of Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) public enlightenment messages into Hausa and other major indigenous languages to sensitise residents ahead of Saturday’s nationwide mock accreditation and results upload exercise. The Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr. Nawani Aboki, disclosed this on Friday while briefing journalists in Lafia ahead of the exercise, saying the grassroots sensitisation campaign was designed to remove language barriers and ensure that rural communities understood the electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections. According to Aboki, the ministry has produced and commenced airing public service announcements listing the 294 polling units selected for the exercise in Nasarawa State. He said radio jingles had also been produced in English, Hausa and local dialects as part of efforts to complement INEC’s voter education campaign, in line with Governor Abdullahi Sule’s commitment to supporting the Commission’s preparations. “This multilingual approach is intended to overcome language barriers and ensure that the message reaches all segments of society, particularly rural communities,” he said. Aboki said INEC had scheduled the nationwide mock exercise for Saturday, November 28, 2026, to test the operational readiness of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Election Results Viewing Portal (IReV), while familiarising voters with the technology ahead of the 2027 polls. He urged registered voters in the state to verify whether their polling units were among those selected for the exercise by visiting INEC’s official website, www.inecnigeria.org. The commissioner also called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, youth groups and civil society organisations to mobilise eligible voters in the selected centres. He urged media organisations to amplify verified electoral information and avoid spreading misinformation, while warning against attempts to disrupt the exercise. “Government wishes to state unequivocally that any individual or group of persons who engages in acts capable of causing political instability, disrupting the electoral process, or inciting violence during this exercise will be dealt with in accordance with the law,” he warned. Aboki added that the state government remained committed to peaceful, issue-based political activities and would continue to partner with INEC and the media to support the conduct of credible and transparent elections in 2027. item.title: Putin unveils new nuclear submarine
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday unveiled a new nuclear-powered submarine and said Russia would add five more to the country’s fleet by 2030, according to footage released by the Kremlin. At the Sevmash shipyard in the northwestern city of Severodvinsk, Putin attended a flag-raising ceremony aboard the Perm submarine, marking its formal transfer to the navy. “Russia is one of the few countries in the world capable of building powerful nuclear submarines of this kind, weapons with global reach and significance,” he said. Nuclear-powered submarines are a key part of Russia’s nuclear deterrent because their ability to operate covertly underwater ensures a retaliatory strike capability in the event of an attack. Putin said the navy would receive five more by 2030, including three vessels from the Yasen-M class, the same class as the Perm. The submarines can operate in “any part of the world’s oceans” while carrying a range of cruise missiles, he added. The post Putin unveils new nuclear submarine appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Keyamo pushes for 99% ICAO safety rating, tasks NAMA, NCAA
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has urged the Nigerian Airspace Management Agency, NAMA, to sustain the country’s improved safety performance through continuous monitoring, institutional collaboration and the systematic resolution of outstanding regulatory requirements. Keyamo commended NAMA for what he described as its exceptional contribution to Nigeria’s impressive performance during the recent International Civil Aviation Organisation ICAO, Coordinated Validation Mission, ICVM. The commendation followed Nigeria’s successful ICVM, conducted between April 15 and 22, 2026, during which the country recorded an Effective Implementation, EI, score of 91.30 per cent. Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Dr Abdullahi Musa, disclosed this in a letter of commendation addressed to NAMA’s Managing Director, Engr Umar Farouk. The minister specifically acknowledged the timely closure of the Significant Safety Concern, SSC, raised by the ICAO team following the validation exercise. He stated: “Keyamo recalled that upon assuming office, one of his cardinal priorities was to ensure strict adherence to aviation safety regulations and sustain a consistent upward trajectory in Nigeria’s ICAO safety rating. “According to him, the 91.30 per cent Effective Implementation score represented a significant validation of the administration’s commitment to aviation safety and had further strengthened Nigeria’s reputation among ICAO Contracting States. “While acknowledging NAMA’s contribution, Keyamo maintained that Nigeria’s improved safety performance must be sustained through continuous monitoring, institutional collaboration and the systematic resolution of outstanding regulatory requirements, even as he urged the agency to collaborate with the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, to address all outstanding Protocol Questions under the Air Navigation Services, ANS, audit area, with a view to raising Nigeria’s Effective Implementation score to at least 99 per cent.” The post Keyamo pushes for 99% ICAO safety rating, tasks NAMA, NCAA appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Naira appreciates to N1,445/$ in parallel market
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira appreciated by N10 against the dollar in the parallel market on Friday, exchanging at N1,445 per dollar, compared with N1,455 on Thursday. Similarly, the naira strengthened in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), appreciating to N1,376 per dollar from N1,378 per dollar recorded on Thursday. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed that the indicative exchange rate in the official market improved by N2 to N1,376 per dollar from N1,378. Consequently, the gap between the parallel and official market exchange rates narrowed to N69 per dollar from N77 recorded on Thursday. Meanwhile, the value of interbank turnover in the NFEM fell by 54.5 per cent to $106.9 million from $235.04 million recorded on Thursday. The post Naira appreciates to N1,445/$ in parallel market appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Osun LG Crisis Will Be Fully Resolved In The Next One Week — Gov Adeleke
item.description: Governor Ademola Adeleke has assured the people of Osun State that the protracted local government crisis in the state will be resolved within the next week, following President Bola Tinubu’s intervention. Governor Adeleke gave this assurance in his inaugural speech during his second-term inauguration held at Osogbo City Stadium, where he listed some of the priorities of his second-term administration across all sectors. “I am glad to announce that Mr President has intervened in the local government matter and in the next one week, the crisis will be fully resolved. Once this is done, our administration will ensure the rehabilitation of the remaining 102 primary health care centres,” he said. Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke was sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. As part of his priorities, the re-elected governor promised to set up the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission, as well as infrastructural expansion and recruitment of teachers and rehabilitation of schools, including reviving technical colleges. He also said that job and wealth creation will be at the heart of his second term. “We will establish a digital hub in each of our three senatorial districts. This is to drive job creation in the digital economy,” Adeleke said. “In education, we will recruit more teachers and speed up school rehabilitation. We will expand bursaries and scholarships, keep tuition affordable, tackle cultism, and revive our technical colleges.” In the health sector, he said about 70 per cent of existing primary health care centres were rehabilitated and equipped with solar and power facilities in his first term. “We upgraded and completed 232 out of 332 primary health care centres. The plan was to complete the whole 332 PHCs, but the seizure of local government allocations halted the process,” the governor said. “My government made sure that our primary school teachers, healthcare professionals at our primary healthcare centres, and local government retirees got paid in the last two years.” Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. Adeleke said his vision is to move Osun from a civil service economy to an industrialised one, noting that his administration is open to partnership with private organisations and economic advisory groups. “Specifically, we will target agro-processing factories, industrial parks across districts, free trade zones, sports and tourism development, and a better business environment. “Fellow citizens, we must heal the wounds of the past and unite for our collective good. I charge the Osun political class to embrace elite consensus, transparency, good governance and local content,” he added. President Tinubu was represented at the inauguration by the Vice President, Kashim Shettima. item.title: [PHOTOS] Adeleke Sworn In For Second Term As Osun Governor
item.description: Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has been sworn in for a second term, beginning another four-year tenure that will run until 2030. Adeleke took the oath of office on Friday, November 27, 2026, at an inauguration ceremony held at the Osogbo Township Stadium. The state Chief Judge administered the oath of office to Deputy Governor Kola Adewusi before swearing in Adeleke. The ceremony was attended by Vice President Kashim Shettima, who led several dignitaries, including former Osun State Governor Bisi Akande, Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa, and former Senate President Bukola Saraki. The entertainment industry was also represented, with Afrobeats singer Davido, alongside B-Red and Shina Rambo, attending the ceremony to celebrate the governor. Adeleke secured re-election in the August 15, 2026 governorship election on the platform of the Accord Party after defecting from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). He polled 511,067 votes to defeat the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, who secured 444,815 votes. Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke sworn in as governor for a second term.
